title: How do I create my first survey in LimeSurvey?
summary: Start a new, empty survey and give it a clear name.
keywords: new create start title welcome settings text elements survey
goal: Create an empty Sustainable Marketing survey without publishing it.
steps: Open your LimeSurvey account
Sign in to the LimeSurvey 3.28 installation supplied by your university.
Choose Create survey
On the LimeSurvey homepage, select the Create survey box.
Give the survey a title
Enter “Sustainable Marketing Research Survey” in Survey Title.
Check the language
Select the Basic Language you will use with your participants. Choose carefully, as the base language cannot simply be changed later.
Add a welcome message
Under Text elements, enter a short welcome message and a brief description, if useful.
Save the survey
Select Save in the upper-right area. LimeSurvey opens the new survey overview.
check: The new survey appears in your survey list.
You can open its overview and see the title.
The survey is not yet activated or open to respondents.
mistakes: I cannot find Create survey
Return to the LimeSurvey homepage. Your university account may also lack permission to create surveys.
I think saving has published my survey
Saving creates the survey design; activation is a separate action.
I cannot change the base language
Check the Basic Language before creating the survey. Additional languages can be configured separately.
verified: Reviewed against published documentation; local 3.28 click-testing and screenshots remain pending

title: How do I add a question group?
summary: Organize related questions into clear sections.
keywords: section add group structure organize order question group
goal: Create a section called Sustainable Marketing Perceptions to hold related questions.
steps: Open your survey
From your survey list, select the survey you want to edit.
Switch to Structure
In the left-hand survey menu, select Structure rather than Settings.
Select Add question group
Choose Add question group from the Structure area.
Enter the group title
In Title, type “Sustainable Marketing Perceptions”. You may add a short description.
Leave advanced fields alone
For this beginner example, leave Randomization Group empty and the default relevance setting unchanged.
Save the new group
Select Save. The group should now appear in the survey structure.
check: The group appears under Structure.
Its title is spelled correctly.
The group is ready for its first question.
mistakes: I cannot add questions
First create at least one question group.
I accidentally used Settings
Switch to the Structure tab in the left-hand menu.
My group is in the wrong position
Use the survey Structure view to arrange groups in the desired order before activating the survey.
verified: Reviewed against published documentation; local 3.28 click-testing and screenshots remain pending

title: How do I add, edit, copy or delete a question?
summary: Learn the main question-editing actions in LimeSurvey 3.
keywords: add edit copy duplicate delete change text question code structure toolbar
goal: Add a simple question, edit its wording, and understand how to copy or remove it safely.
steps: Open the survey Structure tab
Choose the survey and select Structure on the left.
Choose the question group
Select the group where this question belongs.
Select Add question
Use Add question in the structure menu or Add new question to group.
Enter the question code and wording
For example, use the unique code OPEN1 and the question “In your opinion, what should companies do to become more environmentally responsible?”
Choose a suitable type
For that example select Long free text, then Save.
Edit an existing question
Select the question in Structure, then choose Edit from its question toolbar. Make the change and Save.
Copy or delete only when needed
Open the question’s Tools menu to locate Copy or Delete. Check the target and confirmation carefully.
check: The question appears within the correct group.
Its code is unique and the question wording is correct.
You can preview it without changing a live survey.
mistakes: The question is in the wrong group
Check the Question Group setting when editing the question.
The question code is rejected
Use a unique code starting with a letter; avoid spaces and punctuation.
I cannot edit the structure
Some structural changes are restricted after survey activation. Work on a draft copy rather than altering live research data.
verified: Reviewed against published documentation; local 3.28 click-testing and screenshots remain pending

title: How do I save and preview my survey?
summary: See the survey as a participant will see it before collecting data.
keywords: preview test save view inspect check survey question group
goal: Check the wording and layout of a question, group or full draft survey before activation.
steps: Save your changes
In LimeSurvey 3, save after making changes to a question or group.
Open the question or group
In Structure, select the question or question group you want to inspect.
Find the Preview action
Use the toolbar option to preview the selected question or group.
Preview the whole survey
Choose Preview survey from the survey or question toolbar to see the entire draft.
Try different answers
Answer the questions as a participant would. Check wording, available options and navigation.
Return and correct errors
Close the preview, edit the design, save and preview again.
check: Your question is visible with the expected response format.
All necessary answer options appear.
The full survey shows the expected groups and sequence.
mistakes: My preview is not the same as a live response
Previewing helps check the design but is not a substitute for testing the activated survey and stored responses.
A group-only preview shows hidden questions
Group previews may bypass group relevance conditions; always test full survey logic separately.
Changes do not appear
Save the edits, reopen the preview and ensure you are viewing the correct question.

title: How do I create a 5-point Likert scale?
summary: Build a statement matrix with five labelled agreement choices.
keywords: likert five 5 scale strongly agree disagree matrix array subquestions sustainable marketing SMP
goal: Ask participants to rate three Sustainable Marketing Perceptions statements from Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree.
steps: Open the correct group
Select the Sustainable Marketing Perceptions question group.
Add a question
Select Add question and give the parent question a unique code such as SMP.
Choose the flexible Array type
Choose Array, not Array (5 point choice), if you want all five verbal labels to be shown as column headings.
Enter a short question heading
For example: “Please indicate how much you agree with each statement.” Save the question.
Enter the three subquestions
Select Edit subquestions. Use codes SMP1, SMP2 and SMP3, and paste the three statements from the original questionnaire. Save.
Enter five answer options
Select Edit answer options. Use codes 1–5 and labels Strongly Disagree, Disagree, Neutral, Agree, Strongly Agree. Save.
Preview the question
Check that three statement rows and five labelled answer columns appear.
check: All three SMP statements are present.
Each statement has exactly five agreement options.
One answer can be chosen in each row.
mistakes: I see only numbers 1 to 5
The predefined Array (5 point choice) type uses fixed numeric choices. Choose flexible Array when you need five full verbal labels.
I cannot enter all three statements
Edit subquestions: these are the rows in an array.
My data labels are confusing
Use a clear parent question code and recognizable subquestion codes; check exported variable naming before fieldwork.
Labels and stored values

The predefined five-point array uses numeric choices. If you require written choices displayed as Strongly Disagree through Strongly Agree, use a customizable Array question with five labeled answer options instead.
verified: Reviewed against published documentation; local 3.28 click-testing and screenshots remain pending
caution: LimeSurvey 3 has a predefined numeric Array (5 point choice). To display full verbal labels in five columns, use the flexible Array question type with five explicitly labeled answer options instead.

Put each pair in its own question group; name them Pair A, Pair B and so on.

Add a group relevance rule so Pair A displays only for assignment A, Pair B only for B, and so forth.

Check the assignment is stored and stable when participants move backward and forward.
